dedupe_keys.name: hacon hafas journey planning and tps timetable and dispatching software siemens mobility

description: Hacon, part of Siemens Mobility since 2017, develops commercial software for public transport information, ticketing and rail operations planning; it has more than 500 staff in informatics and traffic planning. Its HAFAS.engine trip planning algorithm computes door-to-door routes over buses, trains, trams, ferries, flights, cars, bicycles, scooters and walking, with real-time information, a neutral search that favours no single operator, converters to a uniform data format and a Pareto-optimal search that can weigh vehicle occupancy or arrival reliability; Hacon says it calculates up to 100 million connections a day. The TPS suite covers rail timetable construction (TPS.plan, a digital copy of network and infrastructure with runtime calculation, conflict-free path search and simulation of timetables and operations, using the TAF TAP TSI standard), live dispatching (TPS.live, with conflict detection from real-time train positions) and track works planning (TPS.trackworks). Coverage: generic software used by operators such as TransMilenio in Bogotá and Belgian Railways, per the news items read. Format and access: licensed software and apps delivered through sales and demos. Licence: proprietary; terms and prices were not read. Caveats: public HAFAS interfaces run by individual operators were not checked, and the software was not used. Simulation uses: timetable and operations simulation, disruption dispatching and network-wide journey planning for public transport resilience. Related records: OpenTrack (model-opentrack) and RailSys (model-railsys) are rail simulation tools, and OpenTripPlanner (model-opentripplanner) is an open journey planner.
